clinician.final_diagnosis: Superior Foville syndrome due to pontine hemorrhage
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 20-year-old trader from Senegal with no prior medical history presented with acute onset left hemiparesis that developed 5 days before admission, preceded by acute headaches and rotatory vertigo without nausea or vomiting. On neurological examination at admission, he demonstrated the classic triad of superior Foville syndrome: right oculomotor paralysis (CN VI palsy), right facial palsy (CN VII palsy), and left hemiparesis sparing the face. Brain CT imaging on admission confirmed spontaneous hemorrhage in the right pontine posterolateral region with compression of the fourth ventricle, establishing the structural diagnosis. The patient received conservative management including analgesics, anxiolytics, laxatives, and physiotherapy, with documented clinical improvement. He was discharged after 10 days of hospitalization.
